stanzas: V sadě skví se jara květ,
A to jest ta krásná země -
orig.credit: Josef Kajetán Tyl, Fidlovačka (1834): the song as sung by the fiddler Mareš
orig.page: Fidlovačka, neb: Žádný hněv a žádná rvačka/Obraz čtvrtý

stanzas: Waters thro' its meads are streaming,
Mounts with rustling woods are teeming.
Vales are bright with flowrets rare,
Oh, earth's Eden, thou are fair!
Thou art my home, my fatherland!
Thou art my home, my fatherland!
By the Towers of God 'tis bounded;
True and light of heart are they,
Firm and bold in deadly fray,
Thou art my home, my fatherland!
Thou art my home, my fatherland!
en.credit: uncredited translation from the Chicago University Settlement Song Book, in Charities, vol. 13 (1904)
en.page: Charities/Volume 13/Number 10/The Bohemian National Hymn, My Fatherland
